correctness.rationale: For all probability factors on {0,1,2}, the exact convolution determinant r1*r2*r3-r4*r1^2-r0*r3^2 is b*e times an explicitly nonnegative sum. When TV delta<1/10, all convolution entries are positive and ratio t=r1/r3 is defined. After optional simultaneous reversal t>=1, polynomial nonnegativity forces D=r0/t-r2+t*r4<=0. Two exact dual vectors for 1<=t<=2 and t>=2 give D>0 at delta<1/10. At delta=1/10, strictness and complementary slackness force t=1, r=(v,1/5,3/10,1/5,3/10-v), and polynomial equality yields b*e=0; normalizations give the complete optimizer family. Direct convolution verifies all endpoints. A 4^6 degree-determining exact arithmetic certificate establishes the determinant identity; 9469 assertions pass. All quantifiers, boundaries, normalization, and TV factor 1/2 were rechecked. No numerical experiment substitutes for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Metya and Mukherjee (arXiv:2609.38243v1, 2026-09-29, Section 4.3, Conjecture 4.7) explicitly leave the matching l1 lower bound open for every n>=3 and exhibit only the upper-bound family (their Eq. 22). The new mathematical implication is a rigorous uniform lower bound and exhaustive optimizer classification for the smallest n=3. Asgarli et al. (arXiv:2304.08501v2, Theorem 1) prove optimal squared-Euclidean distance, which does not determine optimal l1 distance or l1 equality. Distinct Wasserstein and KL optima also do not entail this theorem. No equivalence was identified in searches of mathematical research records; priority risk remains for unindexed proofs.

value.rationale: The first open cardinality n=3 of a specific 2026 published finite convolution Manhattan-projection conjecture is completely resolved. The theorem gives an optimal TV constant, identifies every exact factor pair as a one-dimensional interval rather than only giving examples, and shows a structural duality between a nonnegative convolution determinant and sharp TV potentials. This is a natural complete finite classification with unknown prior answer, not an arbitrary special-parameter recomputation. It is of independent interest for approximate uniformity and the loaded-dice model. Future n>=4 cases remain genuinely open.
